What do you guys think about Xenoblade Chronicles X?
I don't own the new Wii U, but if I did I would definitely look into that game.... I'm not even totally sure what the game is about, but Nintendo put up this video to create hype.

C&P from another thread.

If you're playing for the story XCX might not suit. You play as a player-made character, which always reduces the quality of the writing and the emotional investment in the main protagonist IMO (since you have to make a "everyman" character instead of an actual personality), but the affinity missions and your squadmates (especially Lin Lee who is fucking adorable) make up for this somewhat. The story is good.

But the world. Holy shit this world. It is amazing. As far as open world games go, this is one of the most amazing worlds I've ever seen. It's simply beautiful. I've put off story missions simply to go and explore and wander around and see what I can see, to try and climb mountains and look for treasure. It's amazing. If you're an explorer type of player on the Bartle Test, XCX will suit you to a tee.

It's hard for a game to hold my attention these days, but XCX is managing it just fine. I've had it less than a week and am already 35+ hours in to it and I have a giant freakin' robot.

Pros and Cons?

Pros:

Amazing world. Beautiful and vibrant and just wonderful. Open world. Some great characters and decent translation and writing. Interesting plot for a game with a "make your own" main character. So many systems! This game is deep and you can play without even scratching the surface if you want, but if you want to dive in to the details you could drown in them. Absolutely beautiful. No Wii-U game has any right to look this good, considering the console hardware is basically over-clocked last-gen tech.

Cons

The systems, while varied, aren't explained very well in-game, requiring you to read the digital manual for some things, or search the internet for others. Some mission objectives are vague, such as the "collect whatever" and they don't tell you where they can be found. Internet searches fix this but to me that feels like cheating. It takes a long time to get a Skell (but the pay-off is absolutely worth it).

tl;dr, absolutely worth getting IMO. If not for The Witcher 3 it would be my GOTY hands-down.
